# OD → Orca handoff: measured, not guessed

Test date: 2026-11-14 05:14–05:23 (+07).
Worker: Orca agent `opencode` on model `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
Artifact: `design/landing.html` (13,530 bytes) — a full landing page for
"Notewise", generated by OpenDesign and imported into this repo.

## What was actually run

1. Orca agent launched in this worktree, told to call OpenDesign over REST.
2. Agent POSTed a run to `http://127.0.0.1:7456/api/runs` with
   `agentId: deepseek-harness`, `model: opencode-go/glm-5.3`.
3. OpenDesign ran its `od-next-strategy` pipeline and wrote
   `index.html` (13.5 KB) into `od-data/projects/handoff-test/`.
4. The file was copied to `design/landing.html`.

## Timings observed (REST path, strategy pipeline active)

| Job | Result | Wall clock |
|---|---|---|
| Hero section, simple prompt | 17.4 KB `index.html` | ~5–7 min, 2 chained runs |
| Landing page (this file) | 13.5 KB `index.html` | ~6 min, 2–3 chained runs |
| Pitch deck, 5 slides | 26.7 KB `index.html` | ~6 min, 2 chained runs |
| Direct single-file HTML (earlier) | 1.9 KB | ~2 min, 1 run |

The overhead is the strategy stage: OD first runs a "discovery" run, then a
"production" run. A GUI/plugin selection that pins a template skips some of it;
a bare REST call does not.

## The trap that cost 10 minutes

`POST /api/runs` returns a `runId`, but **that run is not necessarily the one
that finishes the work**. The strategy chains continuation runs, and the
original run can sit in `running` while the artifact is already on disk.

A worker that polls `GET /api/runs/<id>` hangs forever. The artifact exists,
the poll never returns `succeeded`.

## Correct recipe for any agent

```sh
# 1. submit
RUN=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7456/api/runs -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{
  \"projectId\":\"my-project\",
  \"clientRequestId\":\"$(uuidgen)\",
  \"message\":\"<what to design>\",
  \"agentId\":\"deepseek-harness\",
  \"model\":\"opencode-go/glm-5.3\"}" | jq -r .runId)

# 2. poll the PROJECT, not the run
until curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7456/api/projects/my-project/files \
  | jq -e '.files[]? | select(.name=="index.html")' >/dev/null; do
  sleep 10
done

# 3. import
cp ../od-data/projects/my-project/index.html design/landing.html
```

Or simply watch the mounted folder — it is a normal path:

```
/home/Mai/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/od-data/projects/<id>/index.html
```

## What this means for the hackathon

* OD is not "slow to think" — it is slow to *finish a pipeline*. Two chained
  runs per artifact is the norm through REST.
* Do not put an OD call inside a component-building loop. Generate the deck and
  the landing page once, commit them, and let Orca workers build from
  `DESIGN.md` + `tokens.css`.
* OD's data dir is bind-mounted at `default-workspace/od-data`, so any agent on
  this machine can read artifacts as plain files — no GUI, no export step.
